title: KM shortlist: SDK tutorial bugs & quickfix log
content:
Date: 2026-03-13
Context: quick working pad for a short prioritized list of doc/SDK issues I want to triage and either patch or hand off. Not a final PR plan, just the stuff I need to clear this afternoon and notes to jog memory later.

Today's high-level goals:
- unblock tutorial flow for new JS users (first-run experience)
- patch 2 small doc examples that surface as runtime errors in v0.9.2 SDK
- prepare 1-liner issue descriptions for triage meeting tomorrow

Quick checklist (prioritized):
[ ] JS tutorial: runtime error when calling stream() in browser example (see repro below)
[ ] Python sample: env var section unclear — needs exact names and export examples
[ ] Embeddings guide: add note about vector dimension mismatch for old models
[ ] Add unit test for the TS example harness to catch the header bug (CI flake)
[ ] Draft PR message + changelog entries for docs repo

Observed issues & repro notes (short):
1) Browser streaming example (docs/quickstart/browser.md)
- symptom: calling client.stream(...) throws "Headers missing: X-Redwood-Client" in Chrome 118 only. Node works fine.
- quick repro: open demo/index.html, click "Start stream"; console: "FetchError: header X-Redwood-Client is not allowed"
- hypothesis: our example sets a custom header from client.ts that is not exposed in CORS example; need to show how to set fetch options or use build-time proxy.
- immediate workaround: change example to use fetch wrapper that sets credentials: 'include' and remove custom header in browser sample.

2) JS SDK example (samples/generate/basic.ts) wrong import path
- symptom: import path uses '@redwood/sdk' but package name is '@redwood-inference/sdk-js' in npm; causes TS compile error for new users.
- patch: replace with "@redwood-inference/sdk-js" and add note about ESM vs CommonJS common pitfalls.

3) Python quickstart env example vague
- symptom: docs show REDWOOD_API_KEY but our SDK actually checks REDWOOD_KEY for legacy compatibility layer. Confusing.
- suggested: standardize on REDWOOD_API_KEY and mention migration layer; give exact export commands for mac/linux and Windows (PowerShell)

4) Embeddings dimension note missing
- symptom: users get shape mismatch when swapping older models that produce 1536 vs new 2048 dims.
- action: add inline table mapping model -> embedding dims in embeddings.md and a small snippet how to reshape/check before sending to FAISS.

Mini reproducible steps (for the browser streaming issue):
1. Clone docs repo: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs.git
2. cd docs/examples/browser-streaming
3. npm i && npm run start
4. Open http://localhost:8080, open console, click stream
5. Observe error: FetchError ... X-Redwood-Client
6. Temporary test: comment out header assignment in src/client.ts -> issue disappears

Suggested quick fixes (what I'll try before handing off):
- Update browser example to avoid custom headers or show use of Service Worker / dev proxy. Minimal edit: remove header, add a note called "Browser CORS note".
- Fix import path in basic.ts and push tiny doc PR with example commit message template.
- Edit python quickstart to include PowerShell export example and call out the legacy env var.
- Add a one-line "embedding dims" table and link to model catalog page before embeddings examples.

Who owns follow-ups (tentative):
- JS streaming CORS example: Kiran (me) afternoon quick patch, QA by Jo
- TS import/path & CI test: Rafael to add unit test and I will review PR
- Python env clarity: assign to Jo - she said she'd tidy the Windows example
- Embedding dims table: create issue and tag research/model-onboarding (for accurate dims), assign to docs backlog owner

Notes-to-self (stream-of-consciousness):
- If I touch browser example, keep changes minimal; want to avoid long philosophical CORS digression in quickstart. Link to an appendix instead.
- Create a single PR that groups 2 semantically related edits (JS import + streaming note) to reduce churn, but separate PR for python and embeddings to keep changelog clean.
- Add line in CONTRIBUTING.md: "Run examples locally: npm run start in examples/<name>" — saves future confusion.

Things to capture in the PR body (template):
- Summary: what broke, who reported, how reproduced (steps), minimal patch and why it's safe, test plan (manual steps), release note (docs: bugfix: browser example CORS)

Open questions / follow-ups for triage meeting:
- Should we standardize env var names or keep compatibility shim? (pros/cons quick list in meeting)
- Do we want to mention default embedding dims in the main quickstart or keep model-catalog as single source of truth?

Slack / Jira links to paste in tickets:
- Slack report thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02ABCD3E/p1700000000000000
- Jira (create ticket under DOCS-321 family)

End of pad. Will draft PRs after lunch and move blockers to the triage board if not completed by EOD.

-- Kiran
